Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 OTE | Reports to Partnerships (GTM partnerships context) |

## JD Complement
This is an ecosystem-scale technical leadership opportunity, not a conventional architecture management post. The central challenge is helping external delivery organizations turn frontier-model capability into dependable enterprise
outcomes.

Anthropic’s market position makes implementation quality part of the commercial proposition. As more enterprise work moves through partners, the company must expand reach while keeping customer expectations, deployment practices, and
responsible-use standards coherent.

The strongest framing is therefore technical leverage: build a partner-facing architecture function that increases ecosystem capacity without creating an uncontrolled layer of bespoke delivery.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic presents itself as an AI safety and research company focused on systems that are dependable, understandable, and controllable. That orientation gives its commercial organization a distinctive constraint: growth must reinforce,
rather than weaken, trust in how its technology is used.

Its model spans end-user business offerings, developer access, and enterprise-oriented adoption. The company also publicly positions cloud, technology, and services organizations as important routes through which customers can solve AI
problems.

This creates an operating model in which product experience, technical implementation, organizational adoption, and partner capability are tightly connected. A weak deployment can affect not only an account outcome but also the market’s
perception of the platform’s reliability and enterprise readiness.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Claude is positioned for knowledge-intensive work such as analysis, software development, writing, and complex problem solving. That creates a broad opportunity set, but broad applicability also raises the burden of identifying where a
solution has clear value, appropriate controls, and a credible path to sustained use.

Anthropic’s enterprise materials treat rollout as a multi-stage process involving technical setup, organizational launch, change adoption, and continuing use. This signals that the company sees value realization as an implementation
discipline, not merely a model-selection decision.

The practical pressure is to make high-quality adoption easier at scale. Partners need latitude to address vertical workflows and customer context, while Anthropic needs common patterns that make security, governance, usability, and
feedback collection repeatable.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic was founded by Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei. Its public-benefit-corporation identity reinforces an expectation that commercial decisions remain connected to beneficial-AI commitments.

The practical stakeholder map likely centers on:
- Partnerships leaders accountable for ecosystem strategy, coverage, and shared commercial outcomes.
- Sales and enterprise teams that rely on partner capability during complex customer evaluations and transformations.
- Product and engineering groups that need structured deployment evidence to distinguish reusable needs from isolated requests.
- Customer technology and business sponsors who must align architecture, governance, adoption, and measurable workflow value.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic’s platform discussion extends beyond prompting or model selection. Enterprise architecture must connect workflow design, integration choices, access controls, evaluation practices, operational monitoring, and adoption
mechanisms.

Its business offering is presented with security and compliance considerations for both business users and developers. That suggests successful partner solutions must account for technical controls and organizational operating models from
the beginning rather than adding governance after a pilot gains traction.

The company’s emphasis on dependable, steerable behavior is also an architecture signal. Reusable patterns should help partners establish appropriate boundaries, validate outcomes, and communicate realistic expectations about model-enabled
workflows.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly identifies services firms, cloud providers, and technology companies as part of its partner network. The ecosystem appears integral to enterprise distribution and implementation capacity rather than simply a source of
introductions.

The publicly described relationship with Accenture illustrates the strategic importance of large services organizations in bringing enterprise-grade AI into customer environments. Such relationships can multiply technical reach, but they
also increase the need for clear readiness standards and repeatable delivery assets.

The ecosystem challenge is to turn partner enthusiasm into consistent execution:
- Build practical learning paths that help technical practitioners identify viable, responsible AI opportunities.
- Establish reusable architectures and solution blueprints that reduce avoidable reinvention.
- Improve technical confidence during important customer pursuits while preserving partner ownership of the delivery relationship.
- Convert recurring field observations into actionable platform, product, and program insight.
- Set a clear quality bar for security, user experience, and deployment discipline across a growing set of implementers.
- Differentiate between scalable enablement needs and account-specific work that should not become a permanent operating burden.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s public enterprise guidance emphasizes organizational rollout alongside technical configuration. That is an important market signal: enterprise buyers increasingly need help moving from experimentation to durable operating
use.

Its partner-facing presence likewise indicates that ecosystem capacity is becoming a material adoption lever. A capable partner can extend Claude into many customer teams and engagements; uneven partner capability can create the opposite
effect.

Urgency is heightened by a competitive AI market in which buyers can assess multiple providers. Anthropic’s advantage will depend not only on model performance, but also on how confidently customers can integrate, govern, deploy, and gain
value from the platform in real operating conditions.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Scaling enterprise AI adoption through services, cloud, and technology partner ecosystems.
- Establishing technical enablement systems that improve partner readiness and delivery consistency.
- Converting platform capabilities into repeatable workflow and industry solution patterns.
- Connecting technical evaluation, implementation design, customer adoption, and long-term value realization.
- Building disciplined feedback loops between customer deployments and internal product teams.
- Leading technical customer-facing organizations through ambiguity, growth, and changing market expectations.
- Combining senior stakeholder communication with practical enterprise architecture judgment.
- Designing AI operating patterns that address governance, security, evaluation, and organizational change.
- Increasing ecosystem technical capacity without allowing strategic work to become unbounded custom services.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic appears to view partner delivery capacity as a major multiplier for enterprise Claude adoption.
- The role appears to sit where ecosystem growth, technical customer confidence, and responsible production use converge.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, achievements, scope, metrics, leadership experience, and technical expertise must come from the governed resume/proof graph.
